DOP has the following advantages: 1) it is a multi-agent policy-based method that supports efficient off-policy training; 2) it addresses the issue of credit assignment in both continuous and discrete action spaces; 3) it is compatible with both discrete and continuous actions; 4) it can be easily extended to support multi-task learning; and 5) it can be extended to support hierarchical learning.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

DOP achieves state-of-the-art performance in both discrete and continous multi-agent settings, and the performance is achieved without the use of centralized critic, centralized value function, centralized training, or centralized execution.
we present a novel off-policy multi-agent policy gradient method that is capable of learning effective joint policies.
DOP is the first MAPG method that achieves the state-of-the-art performance on the StarCraft micromanagement benchmark.
The main takeaway from our work is that
decomposing the value functions into a centralized and decentralized part can improve the performance of MAPGs.
the value function is a powerful tool to improve the performance of policy gradient methods in multi-agent environments.
value function decomposition is crucial to the success of multi-agent reinforcement learning, and it is the first time that the idea has been applied to policy-based algorithms.
